questions: Separate user-selected depth from discovery breadth and stopping criteria.
Evaluate authoritative evidence retrieval, access dates and deduplication without silently omitting requirements.
decision: Maintain a decision-oriented evidence ledger with explicit applicability and refresh triggers; stop research by unresolved decision risk, not source count.
code_observations: studyctl normalizes explicit internal/external study choices and attaches evidence to planning. Its records distinguish questions, sources and synthesis.
The former plan repeated research as a future task even though the user now requests research in advance. Prepared reports should be inputs, not a reason to restart the same literature search.
implementation_steps: Add a compact reusable evidence record with material question, source/version/date, repository applicability, confidence and implementation consequence.
Distinguish verified source facts, observed repository behavior and proposed design. Store failed access attempts and unknowns explicitly rather than substituting a plausible fact.
Deduplicate shared external sources by stable ID while giving each task its own applicability analysis. Refresh only version-sensitive decisions or contradicted evidence.
Use a stopping condition: every high-impact question is answered or has a concrete implementation-time capability probe; no unresolved issue can silently change acceptance.
Preserve user-requested study breadth and the original source. Do not silently narrow a broad study to one blog or use an arbitrary source count as semantic proof.
Record discovery-only, abstract-only and inspected-section scopes separately; do not count inaccessible sources as verified support.
Attach every recommended change to a material question, repository applicability and a falsification condition.
Refresh evidence only on explicit invalidation signals; a task begins from its assigned report rather than restarting the literature survey.
proposed_acceptance_tests: A source with no date/version is flagged for refresh when it affects CLI behavior.
Two tasks sharing the same source retain different applicability notes without copying an entire article.
A contradictory provider document yields a probe requirement, not an invented resolution.
Known prepared reports are consumed without requiring another broad research phase.
A source that was only located cannot satisfy a verified-interface claim.
An API pricing record cannot silently substitute for subscription-quota evidence.
A provider-version change invalidates only affected recommendations, not all 32 reports.

cost_model: For each extra search, compare its expected chance of changing a material decision times avoided rework against search/read cost. This is an engineering stopping rule, not a measured probabilistic claim.
unverified: No complete commercial book was available. This research uses the public AI Engineering excerpt and a public SRE chapter, explicitly labeled as such.
Public material for AI Engineering is limited to the author resource index in this round; no paid book was read. Unknown account-specific facts remain unknown.
runtime_experiments: No authenticated provider invocation, live quota/cost benchmark, independent model review, or Windows runtime test was performed in this research revision.
previous_decision: Turn adaptive study into a bounded decision log: preserve user-selected depth, ask material questions, reuse dated evidence and stop when decisions are stable.
revision_delta: The revision distinguishes search discovery from inspected evidence and introduces a bounded value-of-information rule. Author book resources are not represented as a full-book reading.
decision_analysis: A research record should answer a material design question: what could change the implementation, what evidence bears on it, and what remains unknown. Merely accumulating official URLs does not establish a decision. Preserve the prior conclusion and state whether new evidence strengthens, narrows or reverses it.

Use a shared source register but separate applicability per task. For example, an API cache rule is not evidence about subscription billing in a CLI. A model list proves a listed identifier, not permission, quality, effective reasoning effort or isolated quota. Store those as separate fields with unknown values when necessary.

Repeated broad research during implementation wastes tokens and can make a stable plan drift. Refresh only when a relevant CLI version, source digest, model contract or account capability changes. A retrieved page date and a claim observation date are different; record both when available.

Stop after each high-impact question has an evidence-backed decision or a safe capability-negotiation path. A missing critical fact cannot be hidden in an optimistic assumption. When the alternative would require a costly experiment, define a falsifiable test and a conservative fallback instead of declaring the hypothesis verified.

ownership: This implementation owns its declared write scope and acceptance tests. Its following review checks the actual changed code; prepared research is not acceptance evidence.
baseline_anchor_check: All listed file hashes matched the preserved 0.11.0 source in this revision. This is integrity checking, not a second full code audit.
applicability_rule: Refresh only evidence contradicted by the installed CLI, selected account/billing plan or changed code contract. Unknown required capability blocks that candidate; it does not justify widening permissions.
